approach: Use the authors' released repository directly: clone it, install numpy, run py/run.py once from the repo root to confirm the shipped Iris pipeline works, then write a thin reproduce.py that imports py/LO_K_means.py and drives the authors' K-means and Min-D-LO routines with controlled paired initializations (seeds 0..19, K=5) on data/Iris.txt. reproduce.py only orchestrates the released code and computes the clustering loss externally as the raw sum of squared Euclidean distances, so R1–R14 are satisfied by the authors' implementation rather than a rewrite. It records per-run losses, mean, variance and minimum for both K-means and Min-D-LO in results/metrics.json and checks the paper's C1/C2 values at 10% relative tolerance. A 2-run smoke run proves the data flow before the 20-run full run, which takes seconds on CPU.

files.purpose: Thin wrapper: imports the authors' py/LO_K_means.py, loads data/Iris.txt as raw features, builds 20 paired random initializations (K distinct points sampled without replacement, seeds 0..19), runs K-means and Min-D-LO to convergence, computes raw sum-of-squared-Euclidean loss externally, writes results/metrics.json with per-run losses, mean/variance/min, and pass/fail checks against C1=57.32 and C2=57.54 at 10% relative tolerance. Supports --runs N and --smoke for a 2-run smoke test.

config.initialization: sample K distinct data points uniformly without replacement and use them as initial centers (paper Algorithm 1 Line 1; R3); same initial centers for both algorithms in each run (R11)
config.weights: unit weight for every point (assumption A1)
config.preprocessing: raw Iris features, no standardization (assumption A6)
config.loss_normalization: none; raw sum of weighted squared distances (paper Table 1; assumption A8; R10)
config.convergence: run until assignment vector no longer changes; no iteration cap (paper Sec 5.3.2; assumption A7; R12)
config.tie_break_assignment: smallest cluster index, matching np.argmin (paper Algorithm 1 Line 5; R2)
config.empty_cluster_repair: move the first valid point index from another cluster satisfying s_b(P) > w_g and x_g != c_b (assumption A3; R5; R14)
config.min_d_lo_tie_break: first (n, k2) in nested loop order n=1..N, k2=1..K excluding k1 (assumption A4; R7)
config.center_update: recompute weighted arithmetic mean from current assignments (assumption A5; R1)
config.variance: population variance np.var(ddof=0) of the 20 losses; also report ddof=1 and std for transparency (assumption A10)
config.tolerance: 10% relative on means: accept if |measured - paper| / paper <= 0.10

steps: git clone https://github.com/lmingyi/LO-K-means into ./LO-K-means (if not already present); pip install numpy (already installed, verify import); confirm data/Iris.txt exists and py/LO_K_means.py and py/run.py are present.

Inspect the authors' code without modifying it: print inspect.signature for the K-means and repair functions in py/LO_K_means.py, check how py/run.py loads data, initializes centers, and returns labels/centers/loss. Note the exact function names and whether an initial-center argument is accepted.
Run the authors' shipped entrypoint once from the repo root: python py/run.py, capture stdout, and confirm it produces an Iris table-like result without errors.

Write reproduce.py: load Iris with numpy (space-separated, 4 columns; ignore any label column if present), compute clustering loss externally as sum over n of ||x_n - c_{assignment_n}||^2, use the authors' routines for K-means and Min-D-LO, and for each seed generate K distinct point indices via numpy.random.default_rng(seed).choice(N, K, replace=False), using the same starting centers for both algorithms.

Smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke --runs 2 --dataset iris. Assert finite losses, loss(kmeans) >= loss(min_d_lo) per run (repair only accepts strictly decreasing moves), and print/write results/smoke_metrics.json.

Full run: python reproduce.py --runs 20 --dataset iris. Verify per-run losses are finite, clusters are non-empty with distinct centers at convergence (R14), and record mean, ddof=0 variance, ddof=1 variance, std and minimum for K-means and Min-D-LO.

Cross-check against paper: report measured K-means mean vs 57.54 and Min-D-LO mean vs 57.32 with 10% relative tolerance; write booleans and relative errors into results/metrics.json. If either fails, inspect loss definition (raw sum vs per-point), feature handling, initialization semantics, and whether Min-D-LO was actually invoked after K-means convergence (R6).

Optional verification: confirm the authors' repair routines implement strict-negative acceptance and exact delta (R7–R9, R13) by reading py/LO_K_means.py; do not modify the file. Finalize results/metrics.json as the claim artifact.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke --runs 2 --dataset iris --seed-base 0: two paired runs on all 150 Iris points, K=5, printing per-run K-means and Min-D-LO losses and writing results/smoke_metrics.json; asserts loss is finite, Min-D-LO loss <= K-means loss in both runs, and clusters are non-empty.
intermediate_checks: Iris loads as shape (150, 4) with no NaN/inf and no accidental label column.
Authors' modules import cleanly under Python 3.12 with numpy only; py/run.py completes.
K=5 <= N=150 and each initialization has K distinct indices.
Sanity baseline: first-seed K-means loss should be in a plausible Iris range (roughly 40–120 loss units), not 0 or thousands.
Min-D-LO loss <= K-means loss on every paired run, and repair only runs after K-means assignments stop changing (R6).
At convergence all 5 clusters are non-empty and centers are distinct (R14).
Mean over 20 runs is within 10% of 57.54 for K-means and 57.32 for Min-D-LO; variance magnitudes are of order 10, not 1e-6 or 1e3.
Reported loss is the raw sum over points (not divided by N or K); verify with an independent recomputation from final assignments.
budget_plan: Total ~8 minutes on CPU. Setup 2 min: git clone (seconds), pip install numpy (already present, seconds), inspect authors' code and run py/run.py once (~1 min). Smoke test 1 min: 2 paired runs on Iris. Full run 2 min: 20 paired K-means + Min-D-LO runs on Iris, each <1 ms per the paper, dominated by Python overhead. Verification and metrics writing 2–3 min: recompute loss independently, check non-empty/distinct centers, compare against C1/C2 and write results/metrics.json. No C++ build or large dataset runs are needed for the match target.
